why: Rhein's proposed anti-inflammatory action runs through interleukin-1 and prostaglandin synthesis; cyclooxygenase-2 is the target a modern analgesic comparison would use. Curated as the only relevant target: a measured potency on an unrelated screening target must never stand in for it.
Interleukin-1 beta: diacerein and rhein are described as interleukin-1 inhibitors. Relevance curated, not measured here.
Antispasmodic comparators (dicyclomine, hyoscyamine) act on muscarinic receptors; a carminative comparison would need activity on the same receptors.
Smooth-muscle muscarinic receptor for gut spasm.
Pregnane X receptor: hyperforin's PXR binding is the mechanism of St John's wort CYP3A4 induction (Moore et al. 2000). Relevant as an interaction flag, not as an efficacy target.
